TITLE: Evaluation of Existing Diffusion Planners on Simulated Environments
PROPOSAL: Train and evaluate state-of-the-art diffusion planners (e.g., DeepDream and PLAT) on synthetic datasets of maze navigation, legged robot locomotion, and mobile robot navigation. Metrics: evaluate planned trajectories for feasibility, diversity, and overall quality (e.g., route length, trajectory efficiency) compared to a set of expert demonstrations. Controls: compare to baseline diffusion planners that do not receive prior knowledge of the environment's structure or expert demonstrations. Cost: 50 GPU-hours. Prediction: revealed insights on the strengths and weaknesses of existing diffusion planners on different task domains. Expected failure: if diffusion planners are shown to perform poorly on certain domains, indicating the need for additional research.

Note: We will use a similar framework as "Dreamer" to create expert demonstrations for training the planners during the training phase. For evaluation, a set of random seeds will be supplied to measure how well each planner can generalize and adapt to unseen scenarios.

TITLE: Stitching Method for Learning-Domain Independent Trajectory Models
REVISED PROPOSAL: Develop a hybrid method that combines the strengths of both diffusion-based and stitching approaches for generating long, diverse, and dynamically feasible trajectories. First, apply the stitching method to combine short trajectories from different synthetic environments. Then, utilize a diffusion-based model to refine the stitched trajectories and further increase their diversity and feasibility. Controls: compare the hybrid method to both standalone diffusion-based and stitching-based approaches, as well as a baseline that uses only a single short trajectory. Cost remains estimated at 300 GPU-hours. Prediction: the hybrid method will demonstrate improved sample efficiency and generalization to unseen scenarios, while maintaining or even improving the feasibility of the generated trajectories.

Note: The revision aims to combine the benefits of both approaches, leveraging the ability of stitching to combine diverse short trajectories and the ability of diffusion-based models to refine and increase the diversity of generated trajectories.

PROPOSAL: Provide a theoretical analysis and proof of the conditions under which a hybrid stitching-diffusion method can generate a diverse and feasible set of long trajectories, using a Wasserstein distance-based criterion to measure the difference between the generated and target distributions. Establish a regime where the method is formally guaranteed to produce high-quality trajectories, under certain assumptions about the complexity of the environment and the quality of the input short trajectories. Controls: none, this is a theoretical analysis. Cost: negligible. Compare the performance of the hybrid method to a set of strong baselines, including the best-performing diffusion-based and stitching-based methods. Specifically, evaluate the method's performance on tasks with altered object shapes, sizes, colors, and environmental conditions. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Trajectory Stitching on Diffusion Planners
PROPOSAL: We will explore the effect of trajectory stitching on diffusion planners in maze navigation, using a pre-trained diffusion model on a dataset of short trajectories and then combining them to generate longer ones. We will evaluate these stitched trajectories by comparing their success rates and distances traveled to those generated by the diffusion model without stitching.
CONTROLS: Compare with diffusion model performance on trajectories not stitched together (null case) and evaluate the performance under different stitching methods (e.g., greedy stitching vs. random stitching). We will also compare the quality of the stitched trajectories with those generated by a baseline diffusion planning approach.
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see an improvement in the success rate of the diffusion planner when using trajectory stitching, but performance may degrade if the stitching method is suboptimal (e.g., random stitching).

We expect this experiment to establish a baseline for which any improvements will be compared to in subsequent experiments.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Incremental Trajectory Stitching
PROPOSAL: We extend the single-step trajectory stitching approach by incrementally building longer trajectories from short-segment trajectories, using a likelihood-based online aggregation of segments. This incremental stitching method will allow us to leverage longer trajectory segments as they become available, potentially reducing the limitation of short-segment trajectories on the diffusion model's ability to generate long-term trajectories.
CONTROLS: We compare the incremental stitching method with the original single-step stitching method on performance metrics such as success rate and average distance traveled. We will also evaluate the effect of different stitching intervals (e.g., stitching after every 5 segments, versus every 10 segments) and use the baseline diffusion model performance without stitching.
COST: 15 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Incremental trajectory stitching should allow the diffusion planner to generate longer trajectories with better success rates, while gradually shoring up the limitations of the original stitching method.

This next step aims to enhance the stitching strategy by iteratively adding new segments to build longer trajectories, leveraging the incremental integration of knowledge from the segmentation pool.

TITLE: Meta-Exploration for Trajectory Stitching
REVISED PROPOSAL:  We design a meta-learning framework to explore the stitching weights implicitly, allowing us to robustly learn from trajectories under a range of stitching combinations without explicitly programming the stitching weights. This method, called Meta-Exploration for Trajectory Stitching, will facilitate flexible trajectory combination and exploration and potentially find combinations that were not exhaustively tested by grid search or random search.
CONTROLS:  We compare the performance of our proposed meta-exploration approach with a grid search and random search on stitching weights, on the incremental stitching method (proposed in turn 2), as well as with a baseline model that uses a single fixed stitching approach for all trajectories.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION:  We expect that the meta-exploration approach will perform better than the grid search and random search approaches by finding more effective stitching combinations.
